preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.
The input contains exactly n-1 edges.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints are valid distinct vertices within the range [1, n].
The input edges form a valid tree (connected and acyclic).

postconditions.description: The number of transformations k is between 0 and 2n inclusive.
The number of output transformation lines matches k.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and 1 <= y_prime <= n for x, y, y_prime in transformations)
postconditions.description: All vertices in the transformation output are valid indices within [1, n].

postconditions.expression: all(is_valid_transformation(current_tree, x, y, y_prime) for current_tree, (x, y, y_prime) in zip([initial_tree] + [apply(t) for t in transformations[:-1]], transformations))
postconditions.description: Every transformation satisfies the three conditions: the edge (x, y) exists, the result is a tree, and the component containing x is strictly larger than the component containing y after deletion.

postconditions.expression: sum_squared_distances(final_tree) <= sum_squared_distances(t) for t in all_reachable_trees(initial_tree, max_ops=2*n)
postconditions.description: The final tree configuration minimizes the sum of squared distances between all pairs of vertices among all trees reachable within 2n valid transformations.
